title: Getting Started with UGC
description: Everything you need to know to start your UGC career — what it is, why brands pay for it, and your first-week action plan.
content:
Welcome to UGC — the fastest-growing way for everyday creators to earn money making content for brands. No massive following required. No fancy equipment. Just your phone, your creativity, and this guide.

Let's break down exactly what UGC is, how the money works, and what to do in your first week.

## What is UGC?

**User-Generated Content (UGC)** is content that looks like it was made by a real person — because it was. Brands pay creators like you to make authentic videos, photos, and posts that feel relatable instead of corporate.

Think about it: when was the last time a polished TV commercial made you buy something? Now compare that to a TikTok where someone genuinely loves a product and shows you how they use it. That's UGC.

### Why brands are obsessed with it

The numbers tell the story:

<Highlight emoji="📊" title="UGC by the numbers">
UGC-style content gets **4x higher click-through rates** than traditional ads. Consumers trust real people over brand accounts — and brands know it. That's why the UGC industry is booming.
</Highlight>

- **Authenticity sells.** People trust creators more than ads. A genuine recommendation from a real person converts better than any studio production.
- **It's cost-effective for brands.** A single UGC video can cost a fraction of a professional shoot — and often performs better.
- **Content at scale.** Brands need dozens of creative angles. One in-house team can't keep up. Creators can.
- **Platform algorithms favor it.** TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts all prioritize content that *feels* native to their platform.

### You don't need a huge following

Here's what most people get wrong: **UGC is not influencer marketing.** Influencers get paid for their audience. UGC creators get paid for their content.

You could have 50 followers or 50,000 — it doesn't matter. What matters is:

- You can create content that feels natural and engaging
- You understand what hooks people in the first 3 seconds
- You can follow a brief and deliver on time
- You're willing to learn and improve

<Callout variant="tip">
Many top-earning UGC creators started with zero followers. Brands care about your content quality, not your follower count. Your portfolio is everything.
</Callout>

## Understanding Compensation Models

Before you start creating, you should understand how the money works. There's no single "standard rate" — compensation varies by brand, campaign type, and your experience level.

### Common payment structures

**Flat fee per video** — The most straightforward model. A brand pays you a fixed amount for each piece of content. Beginners typically earn $50–$150 per video; experienced creators can charge $300–$1,000+.

**Revenue share / affiliate** — You earn a percentage of every sale that comes through your content. This can be incredibly lucrative if your content goes viral, but there's more risk since your income depends on performance.

**Product exchange** — The brand sends you free products in exchange for content. This is common for newer creators and can be a great way to build your portfolio — just don't let it become your only compensation model.

**Retainer / ambassador programs** — A brand pays you monthly to create a set number of videos. This is the holy grail: predictable income, ongoing relationships, and less time spent hunting for new gigs. These programs often pay $400–$2,000+/month.

**Performance bonuses** — Some brands offer extra payouts when your content hits certain milestones. For example, a $1,000 bonus if a video crosses 1 million views.

**Referral bonuses** — Many programs pay you for bringing in other creators. If you know someone who'd be a great fit, that's money on the table.

### What to expect starting out

<Callout variant="info">
Be realistic but ambitious. Most brand-new creators start with product exchanges or lower flat fees ($50–$100/video). Within 3–6 months of consistent work, you can push into the $200–$500/video range. Top creators with proven viral track records command $500–$2,000+ per video.
</Callout>

The key is building a portfolio of great work. Every video you create is an investment in your future rates.

## Setting Up Your Creator Profile

Your profile is your storefront. When brands check you out — and they will — your profile should immediately tell them: *"This person creates great content."*

### Choosing a username strategy

You have two main approaches:

- **Personal brand** (e.g., `sarah.creates`, `marcusfilms`) — Best if you want to build your identity across multiple niches. More flexible long-term.
- **Niche-focused** (e.g., `skincarewithsam`, `fitnessbymia`) — Signals expertise in a specific area. Can help you land niche-specific brand deals faster.

<Callout variant="tip">
Pick something memorable, easy to spell, and consistent across platforms. If your TikTok is `@sarah.creates`, grab the same handle on Instagram and YouTube.
</Callout>

### Bio optimization

Your bio gets about 2 seconds of attention. Make them count:

- **Line 1:** What you do. "UGC creator | Skincare & wellness content"
- **Line 2:** Social proof or personality. "Helping brands tell authentic stories" or something that shows your vibe.
- **Line 3:** Call to action. Link to your creator profile or work samples.

### Profile photo best practices

- Use a clear, well-lit photo of your face
- Smile — you want to look approachable and professional
- Avoid heavy filters or sunglasses
- This same photo should appear on all your platforms

### Setting up across platforms

Don't limit yourself to one platform. Set up optimized profiles on:

- **TikTok** — The king of short-form UGC right now
- **Instagram Reels** — Great for slightly more polished content and brand discovery
- **YouTube Shorts** — Growing fast, less competition

You don't need to post everywhere from day one. Start with TikTok, establish your rhythm, then expand.

## Your First Week Checklist

Here's your action plan. These aren't suggestions — they're the moves that separate creators who get results from creators who give up after a week.

<Checklist>
  <ChecklistItem>Complete your ugc.community profile with a great bio and profile photo</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Set up your TikTok account with an optimized username and bio</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Follow 20–30 creators in your target niche (spread it out — don't follow everyone at once)</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Train your algorithm: spend 10–15 minutes daily searching, liking, and engaging with niche content</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Browse the Jobs board on ugc.community for opportunities</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Film and post your first piece of content (it won't be perfect — that's okay)</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Engage with the creator community — comment on other creators' posts, join discussions</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Set a daily content goal (even 1 video/day is a strong start)</ChecklistItem>
</Checklist>

### Training your algorithm

This is the step most people skip — and it's one of the most important.

When you create a new account, the platform doesn't know what content you're about or who should see your videos. You need to teach it.

<Step number={1} title="Search for niche keywords">
Go to TikTok's search bar and look up terms related to your niche. If you're in skincare, search things like "skincare routine," "morning skincare," "best serums," etc.
</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Engage intentionally">
Watch videos all the way through. Like them. Leave genuine comments. Save a few to your favorites. Do this for 10–15 minutes per day for the first 3–5 days.
</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Watch your For You Page shift">
Within a few days, your FYP should start showing more niche-relevant content. This signals to TikTok that your *account* is in this niche — which means your *content* gets pushed to the right audience.
</Step>

<Callout variant="warning">
Don't follow hundreds of accounts at once. Platforms flag this as bot behavior and can shadow-restrict your account. Stick to 20–25 follows per hour max, spread throughout the day.
</Callout>

## What's Next

You've got the foundation. Here's where to go from here:

- **[Platform Setup Guides](/tutorials/platform-setup)** — Deep dive into optimizing your accounts on TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube
- **[Content Creation 101](/tutorials/content-creation-101)** — Equipment, filming tips, and batch recording workflows
- **[Viral Video Formulas](/tutorials/viral-formulas)** — The proven frameworks that get views
- **Browse the [Jobs Board](/dashboard/jobs)** — Start looking at real opportunities

<Callout variant="success">
You're already ahead of 90% of aspiring creators just by reading this far. Most people never get past "thinking about it." You're taking action — and that's what makes the difference.
</Callout>

The path to a successful UGC career isn't complicated. It's showing up consistently, improving with every video, and putting yourself out there. Let's get to work. 🚀

title: Hook Library
description: 30+ plug-and-play hooks organized by category — discovery, transformation, social proof, urgency, and more. Copy, adapt, and use them today.
content:
The hook is the single most important part of your video. You have roughly 1.5–3 seconds to convince someone not to keep scrolling. A great hook creates a **curiosity gap** — the viewer *needs* to keep watching to fill that gap.

This library gives you 30+ proven hooks organized by category. Copy them, adapt them to your niche, and start using them immediately.

## What Makes a Great Hook

Before diving into the library, understand the three psychological triggers that make hooks work:

### 1. Curiosity gap

The viewer knows *something* is being promised but doesn't know *what* yet. They have to keep watching to find out.

> "I just found something that changed my entire routine..."

The viewer thinks: *"What did they find? I need to know."*

### 2. Emotional trigger

The hook connects to a feeling the viewer already has — frustration, desire, FOMO, excitement.

> "If you're tired of trying products that don't work..."

The viewer thinks: *"Yes! That's exactly how I feel."*

### 3. Pattern interrupt

The hook breaks expectations. Something visually or verbally surprising that makes the viewer pause.

> "I'm returning everything I bought this month... except this."

The viewer thinks: *"Wait, what? Why would they—oh, I need to see what they're keeping."*

<Callout variant="tip">
The best hooks combine two or three of these triggers. "Stop scrolling if you've been struggling with [problem]" uses urgency (pattern interrupt) + emotional trigger (connecting to their pain) + curiosity gap (what's the solution?).
</Callout>

## Discovery Hooks

Use these when you're introducing a product, tool, or method to your audience. They position you as someone who found something special.

1. **"I just found the [product type] that actually [delivers on a common promise]"**
   - *Example: "I just found the moisturizer that actually makes your skin glow overnight"*

2. **"Why is nobody talking about this [product type]?"**
   - *Example: "Why is nobody talking about this meal prep container?"*

3. **"I can't believe I just discovered [product/method]"**
   - *Example: "I can't believe I just discovered this way to organize my closet"*

4. **"The [product type] I didn't know I needed"**
   - *Example: "The kitchen gadget I didn't know I needed until now"*

5. **"If you haven't tried [product/method] yet, you need to see this"**
   - *Example: "If you haven't tried oil cleansing yet, you need to see this"*

6. **"I found the [product type] everyone's been looking for"**
   - *Example: "I found the protein bar that actually tastes good"*

## Transformation Hooks

Use these for before/after content, progress updates, or any video where you show a change.

7. **"Watch what happens when I use [product] for [time period]"**
   - *Example: "Watch what happens when I use this serum for 7 days"*

8. **"Before vs. after I started [method/product]"**
   - *Example: "Before vs. after I started using a standing desk"*

9. **"I tried [product] for [time period] — here are the results"**
   - *Example: "I tried cold plunging for 30 days — here are the results"*

10. **"My [routine/space/skin] 3 months ago vs. now"**
    - *Example: "My morning routine 3 months ago vs. now"*

11. **"One change that transformed my [area of life]"**
    - *Example: "One change that transformed my productivity"*

## Social Proof Hooks

These leverage the fact that other people are interested. FOMO is a powerful motivator.

12. **"Everyone keeps asking me about [product/method], so here it is"**
    - *Example: "Everyone keeps asking me about my skincare routine, so here it is"*

13. **"This [product] has [impressive number] reviews for a reason"**
    - *Example: "This blender has 50,000 5-star reviews for a reason"*

14. **"I finally tried the [product/trend] everyone's talking about"**
    - *Example: "I finally tried the viral hair mask everyone's talking about"*

15. **"POV: all your friends already know about this and you don't"**
    - *Example: Works as-is for any product reveal*

16. **"My most requested [product type] recommendation"**
    - *Example: "My most requested book recommendation"*

17. **"The [product] that made my friend ask 'what are you using?'"**
    - *Example: "The perfume that made my friend ask 'what are you wearing?'"*

## Urgency Hooks

Create a sense of immediacy — the viewer should feel like they need to act or pay attention *right now*.

18. **"Stop scrolling if you [relatable problem/desire]"**
    - *Example: "Stop scrolling if you struggle with falling asleep at night"*

19. **"You need to see this before [event/season/deadline]"**
    - *Example: "You need to see this before summer starts"*

20. **"Drop everything — I just found [amazing thing]"**
    - *Example: "Drop everything — I just found the best dry shampoo that ever existed"*

21. **"If you see this, it's a sign to [action]"**
    - *Example: "If you see this, it's a sign to finally start your skincare routine"*

22. **"I almost didn't post this but [reason]"**
    - *Example: "I almost didn't post this but I can't keep this product a secret anymore"*

## Contrarian Hooks

Challenge common beliefs or go against the grain. These create engagement because people either strongly agree or want to argue.

23. **"Nobody talks about [underrated thing] and it's a problem"**
    - *Example: "Nobody talks about the importance of scalp care and it's a problem"*

24. **"Unpopular opinion: [bold statement about your niche]"**
    - *Example: "Unpopular opinion: expensive skincare isn't better than drugstore"*

25. **"Everything you've been told about [topic] is wrong"**
    - *Example: "Everything you've been told about washing your face is wrong"*

26. **"I'm done pretending [popular product/method] works"**
    - *Example: "I'm done pretending expensive gym memberships are worth it"*

## Relatability Hooks

Connect with viewers through shared experiences. These build community and trust.

27. **"POV: you just [relatable moment]"**
    - *Example: "POV: you just found out your skincare routine has been making things worse"*

28. **"Me when I [relatable situation] and discover [product]"**
    - *Example: "Me when I'm stress-eating at 2am and discover healthy snack alternatives"*

29. **"Tell me you [identity/trait] without telling me you [identity/trait]"**
    - *Example: "Tell me you're a skincare addict without telling me you're a skincare addict"*

30. **"Things I wish I knew before I started [activity]"**
    - *Example: "Things I wish I knew before I started working out at home"*

## Product Demo Hooks

Specifically designed for when you're showcasing a product — the bread and butter of UGC work.

31. **"Let me show you why I use [product] every single day"**
    - *Example: "Let me show you why I use this planner every single day"*

32. **"I've tried every [product type] and this is the only one that [benefit]"**
    - *Example: "I've tried every mascara and this is the only one that doesn't smudge"*

33. **"The [product] that replaced [old product/method] in my routine"**
    - *Example: "The app that replaced my physical planner, notes, and calendar"*

34. **"Honest review: is [product] worth the hype?"**
    - *Example: "Honest review: is the viral Stanley Cup worth the hype?"*

35. **"3 things about [product] that surprised me"**
    - *Example: "3 things about this air fryer that surprised me"*

## How to Adapt Hooks for Your Niche

Every hook in this library works as a template. Here's how to customize them:

<Step number={1} title="Identify the structure">
Look at the hook template and find the variables — the parts in [brackets]. These are what you'll replace with your specific content.
</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Fill in your niche">
Replace the variables with products, problems, and benefits specific to your niche. "I just found the [product type] that actually [benefit]" becomes "I just found the moisturizer that actually doesn't clog pores."
</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Test the curiosity gap">
Read your finished hook out loud. Does it make you want to know more? Would you stop scrolling? If not, try a different template or tweak the wording.
</Step>

## Writing Your Own Hooks

Once you've used these templates enough, you'll start writing original hooks. Here's the framework:

**Start with the viewer's desire or pain point.** What does your target audience want? What frustrates them?

**Create a gap.** Promise something without fully revealing it. "I found something..." is better than "I found this specific moisturizer brand."

**Add urgency or emotion.** "Stop scrolling," "You need to see this," "I can't believe" — these phrases create immediate engagement.

**Keep it under 10 words.** Short hooks are more powerful. If your hook needs 20 words, it's not a hook — it's a paragraph.

<Callout variant="info">
Keep a "hook swipe file." Every time you see a hook that makes you stop scrolling, screenshot it. Over time, you'll build a personal library of proven hooks you can reference whenever you need inspiration.
</Callout>

## What's Next

You've got the hooks. Now put them to work:

- **[Viral Video Formulas](/tutorials/viral-formulas)** — Pair these hooks with proven video structures
- **[Community Management](/tutorials/community-management)** — How to handle the engagement your hooks generate
- **[Discoverability](/tutorials/discoverability)** — Hashtags and captions to amplify your reach

title: Platform Setup Guides
description: Step-by-step setup for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts — optimized for UGC creators who want brands to find them.
content:
Your social media profiles are your digital storefront. Before you start creating content, you need to set them up correctly — not just create an account, but *optimize* it so that brands and the right audience can find you.

This guide covers the three major short-form platforms: TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.

## TikTok Setup & Optimization

TikTok is the #1 platform for UGC right now. It's where brands look first when hiring creators, and it's where viral content happens most organically.

### Creating your account

If you're starting fresh (recommended for UGC-focused creators), here's how to do it right:

<Step number={1} title="Choose your username strategically">
Your username is one of the first things brands see. Pick something that signals what you do:

- **Niche-focused:** `skincarewithsam`, `fitfoodsby.ana`, `techreviewsjake`
- **Creator-brand:** `sam.creates`, `ana.ugc`, `jake.films`
- **Personal + niche:** `samantha.beauty`, `ana.wellness`

Avoid random numbers, underscores, or anything hard to spell. You want someone to be able to find you by searching your name.
</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Set up your bio">
Your bio has limited characters — make every word count. Use this formula:

**Line 1:** What you create → "UGC creator | Beauty & skincare content"
**Line 2:** Your vibe or social proof → "Making products look irresistible ✨"
**Line 3:** Call to action → Link to your creator profile or work samples

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Profile photo">
Use a clear, well-lit headshot where your face is visible. No sunglasses, no heavy filters, no group photos. You want to look approachable and professional — this photo will appear on every video you post.
</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Switch to a Creator or Business account">
Go to Settings → Manage Account → Switch to Business Account. This gives you access to analytics and the ability to add a website link in your bio.
</Step>

<Callout variant="tip">
Use the same profile photo and display name across all platforms. Consistency builds recognition — if a brand finds you on TikTok and checks your Instagram, they should instantly know it's the same person.
</Callout>

### Bio formulas that convert

Here are plug-and-play bio formulas. Pick one and customize it:

**The Professional:**
```
UGC Creator | [Niche] Content
Helping brands tell authentic stories
📩 [email] | 🔗 portfolio link
```

**The Personality-Led:**
```
Making [niche] content that actually converts ✨
[Personality trait] creator who loves [interest]
DM for collabs 💌
```

**The Results-Focused:**
```
[Niche] UGC creator
Content that hooks, converts & goes viral
Open to brand partnerships 🤝
```

### Account hygiene

<Callout variant="warning">
New accounts are under extra scrutiny from TikTok's bot detection. Follow these rules to avoid getting flagged:

- **Don't follow more than 20–25 accounts per hour.** Spread follows throughout the day.
- **Don't like hundreds of videos in a row.** Mix likes with watching, commenting, and saving.
- **Don't use third-party automation tools.** They will get your account restricted or banned.
- **Post gradually.** Start with 1 video/day in your first week, then scale up to 2–3/day.
</Callout>

## Training Your Algorithm

This is the single most important thing you can do in your first week — and most people skip it entirely. Training your algorithm means teaching the platform what your content is about, so it knows *who to show your videos to*.

### The technique

For the first 3–5 days, spend 10–15 minutes daily doing this:

<Step number={1} title="Search niche keywords">
Go to the search bar and type terms related to your niche. If you're in fitness, search: "home workout," "gym routine," "protein shake recipe," "fitness transformation," etc.
</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Filter by recent">
Set the filter to "This week" to see fresh, trending content in your niche.
</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Engage deeply">
Don't just scroll. **Watch videos all the way through.** Like the good ones. Leave genuine comments (not just emojis — write something real). Save a few to your favorites.
</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Follow niche creators">
Follow 10–15 established creators in your niche. This tells the algorithm what community you belong to.
</Step>

<Step number={5} title="Check your For You Page">
Within 2–3 days, your FYP should start shifting toward your niche. When 80%+ of your feed is relevant content, your algorithm is trained.
</Step>

<Highlight emoji="🎯" title="Why this works">
TikTok's algorithm uses your engagement patterns to categorize your account. When you consistently interact with fitness content, TikTok thinks: "This is a fitness account." Then when you post fitness content, it gets pushed to fitness audiences — not random viewers.
</Highlight>

### Niche keyword lists by category

Here are starter keyword lists to search and engage with:

**Beauty / Skincare:** skincare routine, glass skin, morning skincare, best serums, skincare for beginners, acne treatment, SPF review, beauty haul

**Fitness:** home workout, gym motivation, protein recipe, workout routine, fitness transformation, weightlifting, yoga flow, HIIT workout

**Tech:** tech review, best gadgets, iPhone tips, productivity apps, desk setup, unboxing, tech haul, app review

**Food:** easy recipe, meal prep, cooking hack, what I eat in a day, healthy meals, budget cooking, food review, kitchen gadgets

**Lifestyle:** daily routine, morning routine, apartment tour, organization hack, self care, productivity tips, minimalism, haul

## Instagram Reels Setup

Instagram is slightly more polished than TikTok — and many brands use it to vet creators. Your Instagram profile should feel curated but authentic.

### Key differences from TikTok

- **Grid aesthetics matter more.** Your Reels appear on your profile grid. Think about visual consistency.
- **Stories are a bonus.** Use Stories to show behind-the-scenes and build personal connection.
- **Brands DM on Instagram more.** Keep your DMs open and check them regularly.
- **Hashtag strategy differs.** Instagram uses fewer but more targeted hashtags than TikTok.

### Setup checklist

<Checklist>
  <ChecklistItem>Switch to a Creator or Professional account (Settings → Account → Account type)</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Use the same username as TikTok (or as close as possible)</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Same profile photo and display name across platforms</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Write a bio optimized for brands: what you do + niche + contact method</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Add your creator profile or work samples link</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Set up your Highlights with categories: "UGC Work," "About Me," "Testimonials"</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Post your first 3–6 Reels before you start reaching out to brands</ChecklistItem>
</Checklist>

## YouTube Shorts Setup

YouTube Shorts is the fastest-growing short-form platform, with less competition for UGC creators. It's also great for long-term discoverability — YouTube content gets searched months and years later.

### Why it matters for UGC creators

- **Search-driven discovery.** People search YouTube for product reviews, tutorials, and recommendations. Your Shorts can rank for these searches.
- **Longer shelf life.** A TikTok might peak in 48 hours. A YouTube Short can get views for months.
- **Brand credibility.** Having a YouTube presence signals professionalism to brands.

### Setup checklist

<Checklist>
  <ChecklistItem>Create a YouTube channel with your creator name</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Upload a channel banner and profile photo</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Write a channel description with your niche and UGC focus</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Add your portfolio link in the About section</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Upload at least 3 Shorts before promoting your channel</ChecklistItem>
</Checklist>

<Callout variant="info">
You can cross-post TikTok content to YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels. Just make sure to remove any platform-specific watermarks first — all three platforms penalize content with competitor watermarks.
</Callout>

## Cross-Platform Strategy

You don't need to be on every platform from day one. Here's the recommended approach:

**Week 1–2:** Focus entirely on TikTok. Get your rhythm, train your algorithm, post consistently.

**Week 3–4:** Add Instagram Reels. Cross-post your best TikTok content (watermark-free) and start building your grid.

**Month 2+:** Add YouTube Shorts. Cross-post top performers and start optimizing titles for search.

<Callout variant="tip">
The goal isn't to be everywhere — it's to be *great* somewhere first, then expand. A strong TikTok profile with 20 solid videos will impress brands more than having 5 mediocre videos scattered across three platforms.
</Callout>

## What's Next

Your platforms are set up and your algorithm is training. Now it's time to create:

- **[Viral Video Formulas](/tutorials/viral-formulas)** — The proven frameworks that get views
- **[Discoverability](/tutorials/discoverability)** — Hashtags, captions, and SEO strategies

title: UGC job brief template for brands hiring creators
description: Write a UGC creator brief with clear compensation, deliverables, eligibility, usage, and application instructions. Includes a copyable template and example.

## What should a UGC job brief include?

A UGC job brief should name the hiring business, describe the product and content needed, state the payment structure, list deliverables and eligibility, explain requested usage, and provide an application destination and closing date. Clear terms help creators assess whether they can do the work before preparing an application.

Brands can [submit a UGC job on ugc.community](/post-job) for free during launch after creating an account or signing in. Submissions are reviewed before publication. The board also includes reviewed external opportunities, labeled separately from jobs posted directly. Submission does not guarantee publication or a particular number of applicants.

## Copy this UGC job brief template

Replace every bracketed field with your actual terms. If a term is still undecided, say so and explain when it will be confirmed.

```text
Role title: [Product category and content format]
Hiring business: [Business name and public website]
Product or service: [What the creator will demonstrate]
Campaign goal: [What the content should communicate]

Deliverables: [Video count, duration, aspect ratios, hooks, raw footage]
Creator responsibilities: [Scripting, filming, editing, posting]
Timeline: [Product arrival, first draft, review, final delivery]
Revisions: [Included rounds and scope]

Compensation type: [Fixed cash, base plus variable, performance only,
                    affiliate, gifted or unpaid]
Fixed payment: [Amount and currency, or state that there is none]
Variable payment: [Conditions and calculation, or none]
Payment schedule: [Trigger, invoicing process, timing, payer]
Product and expenses: [What is supplied and who covers costs]

Eligibility: [Country, language, skills, location, audience requirements]
Usage requested: [Organic, ads, channels, territories, duration]
Posting requirements: [Creator channels and posting duration, or none]
Exclusivity: [Scope and duration, or none]

How to apply: [Form URL or designated application contact]
Application materials: [Samples and information needed to evaluate fit]
Application closing date: [Date and time zone]
Hiring contact: [Business contact for questions]
```

Use a working destination you control and request only the information needed to evaluate an application. Keep confidential campaign materials out of a public listing.

## An illustrative brief

This is a fictional example for formatting, not an open job or a statement about typical pay.

> We need two vertical product demonstration videos for a refillable kitchen spray. Each video should run 20 to 30 seconds and include scripting, filming, and editing. We will provide the product. The fixed fee is $280 USD for both videos, including one revision round per video. There is no performance bonus. We will pay within 14 calendar days after final delivery and receipt of an invoice. We request use on our brand's organic social channels for 90 days after delivery; paid ads, raw footage, creator posting, and exclusivity are outside this brief. Creators must be in the United States for product shipping and able to film in English. The first draft is due 10 days after product delivery.

Before publishing a brief like this, add your real business identity, application destination, hiring contact, and closing date. Confirm that the scope, usage, and payment language reflect the agreement your business intends to offer.

## How should you describe compensation?

Separate fixed payment from possible additional earnings. “$180 fixed fee plus a conditional $90 bonus” communicates more than “earn up to $270.” If compensation is commission only or product only, state that directly.

The board distinguishes guaranteed cash, base plus variable, performance only, affiliate, gifted or unpaid, and unspecified compensation. Read the [creator compensation guide](/tutorials/compare-ugc-compensation) to see how applicants may compare your offer with its workload.

## How does posting on ugc.community work?

1. Create an account or sign in and open [Post a job](/post-job).
2. Submit your business details, brief, compensation, eligibility, usage, application destination, and closing date.
3. The submission enters review before it can appear publicly. If you need to amend a submission, [contact support](/contact) with the company and role title.

Published listings honor their closing dates. Hiring teams manage selection and payment. A reviewed listing is not an endorsement of the employer or a guarantee of results.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is posting a UGC job free?

Job submissions are free during launch. An account is required, and submissions undergo review. This is the current launch policy rather than a promise of permanent pricing.

### Can I post an affiliate or gifted opportunity?

The board has separate compensation categories for affiliate and gifted or unpaid opportunities. Describe the arrangement accurately and submit it for review. Do not label products or potential commissions as guaranteed cash payment.

### Do creators have to post to their own audience?

Only include that requirement if your campaign needs it, and state the channels and duration. Creating assets for brand channels and posting to a creator's audience are different deliverables.

### Can I hire creators through the public API or MCP server?

The [public interfaces](/docs) only read current published jobs. They cannot submit briefs, access private applications, or contact creators. Use the website to submit a job.

## Publish a brief creators can evaluate

[Post a UGC job](/post-job) with the scope and compensation stated clearly. For the applicant perspective, read [where creators find UGC jobs](/tutorials/find-paid-ugc-jobs) and the [application checklist](/tutorials/apply-for-ugc-jobs).

title: Viral Video Formulas
description: The proven frameworks that consistently get views — Hook → Demo → CTA, timing breakdowns, and 5+ fill-in-the-blank templates you can use today.
content:
Going viral isn't luck. It's a formula. The most successful UGC creators don't reinvent the wheel with every video — they use proven structures and adapt them to their niche. This guide breaks down the exact frameworks that consistently generate views, engagement, and conversions.

## The Golden Rule: Copy What Works

Before we get into specific formulas, understand this: **the key to going viral is repeating what already works.**

That's not a shortcut — it's the strategy. Every successful creator studies viral content in their niche, identifies the patterns, and applies them to their own videos.

<Highlight emoji="🔑" title="The viral creator's mindset">
You don't need original ideas. You need original *execution* of proven ideas. Study what's working in your niche, adapt the format, and make it yours with your personality and style.
</Highlight>

### How to study viral content

<Step number={1} title="Find viral videos in your niche">
Search your niche keywords on TikTok. Filter by "This week" and sort by most liked. Save 10–15 videos that have significantly more views than the creator's average.
</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Analyze the structure">
For each video, answer: What's the hook? What happens in the first 3 seconds? How long is it? What's the audio? What text is on screen? What's the call to action?
</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Identify the pattern">
After analyzing 10+ videos, you'll notice patterns: similar hooks, similar timing, similar formats. These patterns are your formulas.
</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Recreate with your twist">
Take the structure and apply it to your content. Same formula, different product/niche/personality. That's how viral content is made.
</Step>

## Formula #1: Hook → Demo → CTA

This is the foundational formula for UGC content. It works across every niche and is what most brands want when they hire a UGC creator.

### The breakdown

**Hook (0–3 seconds):** Grab attention immediately. This is the most important part of the entire video. If your hook doesn't stop the scroll, nothing else matters.

**Demo (3–10 seconds):** Show the product, demonstrate the benefit, or deliver the value you promised in the hook. This is the meat of your content.

**CTA (last 2–3 seconds):** Tell the viewer what to do next. "Link in bio," "Try it yourself," "Comment if you want the link" — make the action clear.

### Timing is everything

| Section | Duration | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 0–3 seconds | Stop the scroll, create curiosity |
| Demo / Value | 3–10 seconds | Deliver on the hook's promise |
| CTA | 10–15 seconds | Drive action |

<Callout variant="tip">
The ideal UGC video is 7–15 seconds long. Shorter videos have higher completion rates, which the algorithm loves. Don't pad your videos — if you can say it in 10 seconds, don't stretch to 30.
</Callout>

### On-screen text timing

Text that appears on screen should last exactly as long as it takes to read. Here's the rule of thumb:

- **Short hook (3–5 words):** 2–3 seconds
- **Medium text (6–10 words):** 3–4 seconds
- **Longer text (11+ words):** 4–5 seconds (avoid if possible — break into multiple screens)

If text disappears before someone can read it, you'll lose them. If it stays too long, the video feels slow. Watch your video back and read the text out loud to check timing.

## Formula #2: Before → After

One of the highest-performing formats across all niches. The transformation creates an immediate visual payoff that keeps people watching.

### Structure

**Before (0–3 seconds):** Show the "problem" state. Messy skin, cluttered desk, bland meal, whatever the "before" looks like in your niche.

**Transition (3–4 seconds):** A quick cut, snap, or swipe transition. Keep it clean and satisfying.

**After (4–8 seconds):** The transformation reveal. This should be visually dramatic — good lighting, close-up, slow reveal if the result is impressive.

### Fill-in-the-blank template

> *"I used to [problem] until I found [product/solution]..."*
> *[Quick transition]*
> *"Now [impressive result]"*

### Works best for:
- Skincare (skin before vs. after product)
- Fitness (body transformation, meal prep)
- Home/organization (messy room → organized)
- Tech (slow workflow → fast workflow with app)

## Formula #3: POV (Point of View)

The POV format creates immersive, relatable content. It puts the viewer *in* a situation rather than watching from the outside.

### Structure

**Text overlay:** "POV: [relatable scenario]"

**Visual:** You acting out the scenario — facial expressions, body language, and reactions.

**Audio:** Trending sound that matches the mood, or original voiceover.

### Fill-in-the-blank template

> *"POV: you just discovered [product/tool] and your [specific area of life] is about to change forever"*

> *"POV: your friend asks how you always [impressive result] and you show them [product]"*

> *"POV: it's your first week using [product] and you already [benefit]"*

### Tips for POV content

- **Facial expressions sell it.** Exaggerate slightly — surprise, excitement, satisfaction. The camera flattens emotion, so dial it up by 20%.
- **Keep it under 10 seconds.** POV content should be quick and punchy.
- **Use trending audio that matches the emotion** of your scenario.

## Formula #4: Storytelling Micro-Format

Short-form storytelling is incredibly powerful. You're not telling a novel — you're telling a 15-second story with a setup, tension, and payoff.

### Structure

**Setup (0–3 seconds):** "I almost didn't try [product], but..."

**Tension (3–8 seconds):** Build the middle. What happened? What changed? What was unexpected?

**Payoff (8–12 seconds):** The satisfying conclusion. The result, the revelation, the recommendation.

### Fill-in-the-blank template

> *"I was skeptical about [product/method] but after [time period], [impressive result happened]"*

> *"Everyone told me [common belief] but then I tried [alternative approach] and [surprising outcome]"*

> *"I've tried every [product category] and nothing worked until [specific product/method]"*

## Formula #5: Reaction / Response

React to content, comments, or trends in your niche. This format is great because it rides existing viral content — you're essentially borrowing someone else's audience.

### Structure

**Setup:** Show the original content, comment, or trend you're reacting to.

**Reaction:** Your genuine response — surprise, agreement, breakdown, or counter-opinion.

**Value add:** What can you add that the original didn't? Your expertise, experience, or perspective.

### Types of reaction content

- **Stitch / Duet:** React to another creator's video with your take
- **Comment reply:** Film a video response to a viewer's comment (builds engagement loops)
- **Trend response:** Put your niche spin on a trending format

## Formula #6: The "Secret" / Discovery

People love feeling like they're getting insider knowledge. This formula positions your content as a discovery or secret that most people don't know about.

### Fill-in-the-blank templates

> *"I just found the [product/tool] that [impressive benefit] and I can't believe more people don't know about it"*

> *"Why is nobody talking about [product]? It literally [specific benefit]"*

> *"The [product category] hack that changed my entire [routine/workflow/life]"*

> *"I've been keeping this secret for [time] but I have to share [product/method]"*

> *"If you're still using [old method], you NEED to see this"*

## The Hook + Expression Combo

Across all formulas, there's one technique that consistently boosts performance: **pairing your hook text with an expressive facial reaction.**

### How it works

In the first 1–3 seconds of your video:

1. **On-screen text:** Your hook appears (e.g., "I just found the best thing for my skin")
2. **Your face:** Shows a matching emotion — surprise, excitement, awe, shock
3. **The combination:** Creates curiosity. Viewers see text + emotion and think "I need to know what they're talking about"

<Callout variant="tip">
Practice your "hook face" in the mirror. The three most effective expressions for UGC:

1. **Wide-eyed surprise** — eyebrows up, mouth slightly open
2. **Excited smile** — genuine enthusiasm, like you just discovered something amazing
3. **Skeptical-then-impressed** — start doubtful, shift to surprised (works great for before/after)

These expressions need to feel natural. Watch your favorite creators and notice how they use facial expressions in their hooks.
</Callout>

## Pattern Interrupts & Retention Techniques

Getting someone to *start* watching is only half the battle. You also need to keep them watching until the end. High completion rates = more reach from the algorithm.

### Text progression

Don't show all your text at once. Reveal it progressively:
- Screen 1: "I found something..."
- Screen 2: "...that completely changed..."
- Screen 3: "...my morning routine"

This creates micro-curiosity loops within the video.

### Visual movement

Static videos lose attention. Keep things moving:
- Walk toward the camera while talking
- Pick up and show the product with your hands
- Use quick cuts between different angles
- Point at text on screen

### The "wait for it" technique

If your video has a big reveal, build anticipation:
- "Watch what happens when I..."
- "Wait until you see the result..."
- A brief pause before the reveal creates tension

### Loop your video

Make your last frame connect seamlessly to your first frame. When a video "loops" naturally, viewers watch it multiple times without realizing it — and rewatches count as views.

## Putting It All Together

Here's a practical workflow for creating a video using these formulas:

<Checklist>
  <ChecklistItem>Choose your formula (Hook→Demo→CTA, Before→After, POV, etc.)</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Write your hook — what text will appear in the first 3 seconds?</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Plan your "hook face" — what expression matches the emotion?</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Outline the middle section — what value are you delivering?</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Decide your CTA — what do you want viewers to do?</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Choose your audio — trending sound or original voiceover?</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Film 2–3 takes and pick the most natural one</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Add on-screen text with proper timing</ChecklistItem>
  <ChecklistItem>Watch it back — would YOU stop scrolling for this?</ChecklistItem>
</Checklist>

## What's Next

You know the formulas. Now you need the hooks to power them:

- **[Hook Library](/tutorials/hook-library)** — 30+ plug-and-play hooks categorized by type
- **[Content Creation 101](/tutorials/content-creation-101)** — If you haven't set up your filming setup yet
- **[Discoverability](/tutorials/discoverability)** — Hashtags, captions, and getting your content seen
